title: Transfer binary reference contraction to a complete Bell record with its real success prior
statement: Complete J(X)=PXP tensor|0><0|+(I-P)X(I-P)tensor|1><1|, then retain only its flag passed through BSC(epsilon). N994 applies to arbitrary finite reference operator weights at the actual prior p; for p=1/6,epsilon=1/4 the sharp coefficient is log2/(2log5), rather than the balanced-prior1/4.

provides: Complete J(X)=PXP tensor|0><0|+(I-P)X(I-P)tensor|1><1|, then retain only its flag passed through BSC(epsilon). N994 applies to arbitrary finite reference operator weights at the actual prior p; for p=1/6,epsilon=1/4 the sharp coefficient is log2/(2log5), rather than the balanced-prior1/4.

body: Kraus completeness makes J a channel on every entangled reference. After tracing quantum output, write unnormalized reference weights A0,A1, whose mixtures under BSC satisfy exactly the binary N994 hypotheses. For bias b=|1-2p| and lambda=1-2epsilon, the scalar fixed-prior coefficient is lambda*atanh(lambda*b)/atanh(b), with balanced limitlambda^2. Its Bregman proof has equal minima at opposite biases. N993's two coefficient balances cancel exactly, giving the same coefficient for noncommuting weights. At p=1/6,epsilon=1/4 it is log2/(2log5). The canonical far-pair weights A_success=P_far/6 and A_failure=I4/4-P_far/6 are positive and have the actual prior. This is a documented compatible interface at the cited old Astra version, not a wording analogy or new held-out discovery.
